prs.title: fix(migrations): renumber pr_needs_attention_wakeup 610 -> 622 (CHE-1610)
prs.body:
**Status:** Draft until the fresh review and OCR receipt exist for head `34bdb98122290e2981fb51f60edb53ac4d47077f`. Fixes the red `main` CI at `ca0e11c49`.

**Change:**
- Renames `610_pr_needs_attention_wakeup` (up and down) to `622_pr_needs_attention_wakeup`. The SQL is unchanged.
- PR #184 (CHE-1417) added this migration after PR #193 had already taken prefix 610 with `610_decision_class_change_request_index`. `TestMigrationNumericPrefixesAreUnique` fails on that duplicate.
- 622 skips 619, 620 and 621. Open PRs #218 and #220 already use those numbers.

**Conditions:**
- The runner records the full file stem, not the number. The duplicate does not break the runner itself. It fails the `backend` check, and CD admission requires `backend` success, so no `main` head after `ca0e11c49` can deploy to C00 until this merges.
- A database that already applied `610_pr_needs_attention_wakeup` runs `622_pr_needs_attention_wakeup` once more. The SQL is idempotent: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` and a drop and re-add of the same CHECK constraints.

**Evidence:**
- Local: `go test ./internal/migrations/ -run 'TestMigrationNumericPrefixesAreUnique|TestMigrationFilesHaveMatchingDirections'` passes.
- Local, throwaway database on X99 Postgres: a full `go run ./cmd/migrate up` applied `622_pr_needs_attention_wakeup`. Then the `622` row was renamed to `610_pr_needs_attention_wakeup` to copy a database that ran the old stem. A second `up` re-applied `622` with exit 0, and `issue_wakeup_system_rule_check` still includes `pr_needs_attention`. The throwaway database was dropped.

- Rollback restriction (OCR-221-1, P2, accepted as non-blocking by the reviewer and the dev team leader): on a database that already holds the old `610_pr_needs_attention_wakeup` row, `migrate down --to 618_decision_comment_request_validate` runs the 622 down file. It deletes existing `pr_needs_attention` wakeup data and drops `snapshot_base_ref`, while the 610 row stays. Such a database uses a manual rollback instead. C00 has 0 rows for the 610 stem (read-only check, 2026-10-13 18:11 ICT), so the restriction does not apply to C00.

Refs CHE-1610

prs.title: revert(chat): remove lane summaries and turn reminder [squash]
prs.body:

Code-removal phase on `main`, now reconciled with `03e01212ec0dc8d091e81c38c24be8c7ef4678e9`. Ready for review: Sonnet signed a PASS on head `ebd8836b`. Merge stays Cheese's.

## Conditions
- This PR contains no column-drop migration. Both live summary columns remain, so the old colour keeps working during migration-before-cutover deployment.
- The generated queries do not reference either retired column. An offline sqlc schema input keeps regeneration column-independent without executing DDL.
- Migration 619 is in https://github.com/cheese-work/multica/pull/218. Merge that follow-up only after this PR is deployed to C00. The drop raises the rollback compatibility floor.
- No merge, deployment, live migration, daemon update, or changes to the CHE-1559/CHE-1587 layer branches occur here.

## Change
- Remove the DM reminder.
- Remove the task-claim summary metadata/count query.
- Remove the summary CLI/API and session response/client fields.
- Remove the summary fence and writer validation now merged from #211.

Preserve Chat read authorization and continuation summaries. Preserve continuation unread behavior and DM rename. Preserve decision intents and mention-snippet listing from current `main`.

Keep migrations 596 and 615 through 618 unchanged. Runtime migrations stop at 618. sqlc reads the separate offline schema input; the migration runner does not.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  DB["Database: summary columns retained"] --> Query["Generated queries: no summary columns"]
  Query --> Claim["Daemon task claim"]
  Claim --> Prompt["DM prompt: no summary upkeep"]
  Query --> API["Session read APIs"]
  API --> Clients["Web/desktop session schemas"]
```

## Evidence
- The projection regression fails after a naive migration split regenerates summary-column reads. The offline schema input makes the regression pass.
- `make sqlc` regenerates without drift.
- See CHE-1610 for current-head race-test results and OCR receipts. The prior Sonnet PASS is not approval of this changed head.

Refs CHE-1610
PR #218 carries the remaining column drop and the close intent for CHE-1610.

Closes CHE-1627

prs.title: feat(chat): full-copy DM forks with an optional first message (CHE-1626)
prs.body:
## Status

Draft. The head implements the full-copy fork from the approved `/fork` spec rev 3 (CHE-1606 comment 01a13561-936b-7d57-a1f2-21f391d3516a).
The cross-lab PASS on `e098ba68b4905b170fb71253c8b6a8c2e6a86799` does not cover this head. This head needs a new independent review from outside the Anthropic lab.
CI on head `9727d15062a1715210e5e5e5d91a262e85367f1a` (main merged in, including PR #221): at 23:24 ICT every finished check passes; `backend-tests` is still running. Locally, `TestMigrationNumericPrefixesAreUnique` passes and `620_`, `621_` and `622_` are each used once.

## Conditions

Build and test on X99 only. No merge, release or deploy is authorized. Agents never merge.
Approval: Cheese approved spec rev 3 at about 19:45 ICT on 13 Oct 2026.
Amendment author: x99-claude-opus, after three x99-codex-sol runs failed with model-endpoint 503 errors. The author does not sign the review of this PR.
Keep this PR draft until the independent reviewer signs PASS.

## Change

- **Full copy, no summary.** One transaction copies every member-visible message of the source into a new child DM. The copy keeps role, text, kind, original time, elapsed time and failure text. Copies have no task, no quick actions and no channel fields. Not copied: the onboarding kickoff, queued follow-ups, channel commands, and rows with no text, no failure text and no attachments. The onboarding opening becomes an ordinary message. New IDs follow source order.
- **Attachments.** Source attachment rows are read `FOR SHARE` and copied onto the same stored files with new IDs. Download links in copied text are rewritten to the new IDs. Deleting an attachment row keeps the stored file while another row in the workspace refers to it. The check runs in the delete transaction.
- **Request contract.** Session-human body: a required `idempotency_key` and an optional `message`. A `summary` field returns 400. With a message, the same transaction inserts it as the child's first user message and enqueues the first turn through the normal web DM send path. A failed insert or enqueue rolls back the whole fork. A task-scoped fork takes no message (400). Its default key is `chat_input_task_id`, with the task ID as fallback, so an auto-retry of the turn returns the same child. A replay returns 200, the same child and the stored message, and copies or sends nothing.
- **Rejections.** An empty source returns 409 "nothing to fork yet". Agent-builder, archived, channel-origin and channel-bound DMs return 409.
- **Migration 620 (amended in place).** Adds `fork_last_message_id` and `fork_message_count`. `last_read_at` is the newest copied time, so the copy counts as read. Session responses and both lists expose the fields. The core schema parses them.
- **Title.** "<source> (fork: <message>)": the message is trimmed, whitespace collapsed and cut at 40 characters with "…". Without a message the title is "<source> (fork)". The first send in a fork child does not auto-title it.
- **DM list order.** Both creator lists order by the later of the last-message time and the session creation time, so a new fork of an old DM lists first.
- **OCR fixes on `3fa405d2930969a3b32b4cf9281eae08c313e74a`.** OCR-220-1 (P1): the attachment index now cuts each file name to 255 bytes and the index to 16 KiB, keeps the omitted count, and the block stays within 64 KiB. OCR-220-2 (P2): the first message moves just after the newest copied row, and the replay finds it through its task, created in the fork transaction.
- **Fork context block.** A fork child never reads a continuation summary. On a claim with no provider session to resume, the server prepends a fork notice, an index of copied attachments (at most 100, newest first) and the DM transcript inside `<fork_history>` delimiters. The transcript keeps the newest whole messages within 64 KiB and renders slash-skill links as plain labels. When messages are left out, the block states "the last K of N" and points to `multica chat history`. A resumed provider session gets no block. The shared-directory sentence appears only when the project has a local directory.
- **CLI.** `chat continue --fork` sends no summary and rejects `--summary-file`. Fork errors start with "fork chat:". `--help` contrasts archive and `--fork`. Plain `continue` is unchanged.
- **Docs.** `cli.mdx` describes the full copy, the block and the message.

`/compact` (`chat_continue.go`) is byte-identical to main.

Source-link decision (unchanged): a separate `forked_from_session_id`. `continued_from_session_id` is not reused, because a fork leaves the source active and allows several children.

Choices where the asks left room:
- The CLI has no `--message`. The CLI only reaches the task-scoped endpoint, and a task-scoped fork takes no message.
- A normal chat send has no message size limit. The fork body is capped at 1 MiB. A larger body returns 400. The cap covers the whole body: the handler reads past the request object to the end, so trailing bytes beyond 1 MiB, or any trailing JSON, return 400.
- A message is cut at a UTF-8 boundary only when the newest message alone exceeds the block cap. Otherwise older messages are left out whole.
- The replay finds the stored first message by the child's creation time. The fork writes both in one transaction.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Web or CLI
    participant API as Fork API
    participant DB
    participant Daemon
    Client->>API: idempotency_key, optional message
    API->>DB: lock source, look up key
    alt key exists
        DB-->>API: stored child and message
        API-->>Client: 200, nothing copied or sent
    else new key
        API->>DB: copy messages and attachments, set fork fields
        opt message given
            API->>DB: insert first message, enqueue first turn
        end
        API-->>Client: 201 child, message
    end
    Daemon->>API: claim child turn
    API-->>Daemon: fork block, then the current message
```

## Evidence

Head: `9727d15062a1715210e5e5e5d91a262e85367f1a`, with main `859bf118c6450fdef2cf8394667b83a619cc6d75` merged in (merge commit, no rebase).
All runs on X99 against the isolated, freshly migrated database `multica_che1626_opusamend`.

TDD, failing test before each change:
- Body cap (verifier P2 on `982c887d58841e9310af75852ab07d2b0379db81`): tests-only commit `89e9cc091e7eef6e7ef364800141b0e7e97c7f39` fails against its parent. Fix commit `d2fd534e68efa158f408d8e759a4f642571b2b06` makes it pass. Failing output:

```text
--- FAIL: TestForkChatSessionRejectsBodyPaddedPastTheCap (0.04s)
    chat_fork_test.go:751: POST /api/chat/sessions/e22f2531-f2a0-429a-bfc9-57d22dd407f0/fork: expected 400, got 201
```
0. OCR fixes: 100 attachment names of 1 KiB and one 72 KiB name produce a 182,819-byte block. A copied row newer than the fork transaction sorts after the first message. Then 15 fork tests, including 4 claim tests, pass.
1. Fork contract: 7 fork tests fail against a 501 stub. The copy test first failed on a fixture error. A later stub run shows its 501. Then they pass.
2. Claim block: the fork-child claim fails with 500 "failed to load continuation summary". The capped test shows a copied continuation summary as the whole 61-byte block. Then 3 claim tests pass.
3. Shared file: a delete that waits for the fork's share lock removes the stored file. Then the file is kept until the last row goes.
4. List and title: the new fork lists below an older DM. After the order fix, the first send retitles the fork "Generated Title". Then both pass.
5. CLI: `--help` lacks the contrast, and `--fork --summary-file` is not rejected before HTTP. Then 4 CLI tests pass. Core schema: a malformed `fork_last_message_id` is kept. Then 496 core API tests pass and core typecheck passes.

Suites on the head:
- `go test ./internal/handler`: PASS (full package, 135 s). 49 tests skip: 39 need `REDIS_TEST_URL`. No fork or continuation test skips. The earlier "0 skips" claim counted non-verbose output, which prints no skips; it was wrong.
- `go test -race` on the fork, continuation, `/compact`, send, title and delete tests: 37 PASS.
- `go test ./internal/service ./cmd/migrate`: PASS. `./internal/daemon` and `./cmd/multica`: PASS with the runtime's `MULTICA_*` variables unset. `./cmd/multica` ran in a copy outside the live task marker.
- Migration `620`/`621` down to 618 and up again: PASS. `go vet ./...`: clean. `golangci-lint run ./... --new-from-merge-base=origin/main`: 0 issues. sqlc regenerate: no diff.
- Copy of 2,000 messages of 4 KiB with 200 attachments: 0.46 s to 0.48 s over 3 runs (`TestForkChatSessionCopiesLargeDM`).
- `TestMigrationNumericPrefixesAreUnique`: FAIL only on the duplicate `610` migrations from main.

Not run: Playwright, frontend views tests (layer 3 owns the web UI), GitHub Mermaid rendering.

**AI disclosure:** amendment by x99-claude-opus (Anthropic), Claude Code. Earlier commits by x99-codex-sol (OpenAI), Codex CLI 0.155.1. No force-push or merge.

Closes CHE-1626
Refs CHE-1605

prs.title: feat(chat): rename a DM without an agent turn (CHE-1607)
prs.body:
## Status

Draft correction candidate: `3d61ae2fa5a86e9d52c8347220fbe9052915ed35`.
Independent final verification and the exact-head OCR receipt are pending.

## Conditions

- No merge, release, deploy or C00 build is authorized.
- Keep the PR draft until x99-claude-opus signs PASS and addresses every OCR P0/P1.
- Approval remains Cheese's chat decision at 12:46 ICT on 13 Oct 2026, "start one at a time" (CHE-1527), for CHE-1604 layer 1. Original estimate: four hours or less.
- Server-ignore decision: do not ignore `/rename` on the server. A leaked command remains an ordinary agent message. No server contract changes are needed.
- Title validation matches inline rename. Trim whitespace. Reject more than 200 UTF-16 code units. Skip unchanged titles. A bare command opens inline editing.

## Change

- Offer first-word-only `/rename [title]` beside `/compact` only when the composer has `onRename`. The agent builder no longer advertises an unsupported command. Localized descriptions and Multica styling remain in all five supported locales.
- Read the title from the production editor's plain text, not its Markdown serialization. Literal `_`, `*`, brackets and `<` remain literal. Collapse paragraph and hard-break newlines to a single-line title.
- Intercept rename in the shared DM composer for both web/desktop chat-page and floating-window surfaces. Reuse the existing title mutation and its shared-cache update/rollback.
- Clear only the unchanged submitted draft after success. Preserve failed commands, mid-flight typing and another session's draft. Bare rename selects the current inline title without refocusing the composer.
- `/compact` continues through its existing send path unchanged. Composers without `onRename` retain ordinary sending for manually typed `/rename` text. Menu capability updates without remounting the editor.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Composer[DM composer] --> Intercept{First word is /rename?}
    Intercept -->|No| Send[Existing chat send]
    Intercept -->|Yes| Title{Title supplied?}
    Title -->|No| Inline[Existing inline rename field]
    Title -->|Yes| Update[Existing UpdateChatSession mutation]
    Update -->|Success| Clear[Clear unchanged submitted draft]
    Update -->|Failure| Keep[Show error and keep draft]
    Inline --> Clear
```

## Evidence

- Real-editor TDD red: restoring the original interceptor produced 3 failed and 3 skipped tests. The failures showed escaped title characters and retained paragraph/hard-break newlines.
- Green: the six real-editor regressions passed. The six targeted files passed 186 tests.
- `pnpm exec turbo test --filter='@multica/views' -- --shard=1/2 --maxWorkers=4` passed 3,116 tests across 241 files.
- The default-worker shard first timed out in two untouched tests: `autopilot-dialog.validation.test.tsx` and `table-view-editing.test.tsx`. Both files and `chat-queue.test.tsx` then passed in isolation: 20 tests. The cause is not proven.
- `pnpm typecheck` passed all 10 frontend workspace tasks. Mobile is excluded by the existing root command.
- Scoped ESLint passed with zero errors and one existing `inFlightUploadsRef.current` cleanup warning. `git diff --check` passed.
- New-head CI passed: 11 SUCCESS checks and 8 SKIPPED checks. Both `frontend-views-test (1/2)` and `frontend-views-test (2/2)` passed. Run: https://github.com/cheese-work/multica/actions/runs/38361294133.
- Server tests and live-app E2E were NOT-RUN locally. No server code changed. Mermaid syntax and local headless Chromium rendering passed. GitHub rendering is NOT-RUN.

Closes CHE-1607
Refs CHE-1604
